narrative.overview:
The counter runs on the board behind the desk. Prices are written up in marker, grouped in columns by facility; today's sales are written down underneath as they happen; and every record that is waiting on someone carries a magnet. The interface is that board made electronic — a white field with a faint printed grid, marker-hued headings, thick marker rules between sections, and one amber marker reserved for the action that takes money.

The colour system is the board's own logic. Four marker hues name the four things the club sells access to — blue for swimming, green for the gym, orange for the steam room, purple for a combination — and they appear as a stripe across the top of a price tile, as a dot beside a name, and nowhere else. Five magnets name the state of a record: done, pending, rejected, informational, and off. Those two systems, plus amber for a commitment, are the entire saturated palette; everything else is ink on board with one hairline.

The scale is a counter's, not a showroom's. The reference screen is a 1366×768 laptop with a queue at the desk, so controls are 36px, the content pane pads at 12px, and tables run at a compact ledger density tuned line by line for Khmer. Secondary text is deliberately darker than a stock theme would set it, and the caption step carries extra line height, because Khmer stacks subscript consonants that crowd the line beneath. Both faces are bundled with the app; the counter never waits on a network to render a price.
keyCharacteristics: A white board with a printed 24px grid, ruled off in 2px marker between sections.
Four marker hues for facilities, five magnets for record state, one amber for the commitment.
Marker weight is real weight: headings and prices are set at 900.
Compact by design — 36px controls, 12px page padding, a ledger table density.
Khmer-tuned contrast and line height, on screen and on the printed slip.
Light-only, laptop-first, with the printed slip as its own paper world.

rules.name: The Facility Rule
rules.body: Blue, green, orange and purple mean swimming, gym, steam and combination — on a tile, a price row, a chip, a report column. They are never chosen per page for variety, and they are defined exactly once, in `frontend/src/lib/facility.ts`. A page that declares its own facility palette is a defect; there were three such copies before this system existed.

rules.name: The Two Systems Rule
rules.body: A marker hue says what something *is*; a magnet says what state it is *in*. They never swap jobs. A record's status is never coloured with a facility hue, and a facility is never represented by a magnet colour.

rules.name: The Ink Text Rule
rules.body: Gym green and steam orange do not clear 4.5:1 on white, so no sentence, label or table cell is ever set in a marker hue. Marker colour lives in dots, stripes and the large price figure; the words stay ink.

rules.name: The One Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber marks the committing action and nothing else — never a heading, a border for emphasis, a chip, or an answer to "this looks plain". It is also the only place in the product where a colour carries ink lettering rather than white, and that is deliberate: the contrast floor decides the lettering, not the convention.

rules.name: The Legible Khmer Rule
rules.body: Soft ink stays at 38% lightness. Lightening it back toward a stock theme's default for Latin taste breaks Khmer at caption size.

rules.name: The Caption Floor Rule
rules.body: `text-caption` at 0.75rem is the smallest type on screen. Arbitrary `text-[Npx]` sizes are drift; the printed slips are the sole exception, because they are paper calibrated to a thermal raster rather than to this ramp.

rules.name: The Marker Weight Rule
rules.body: Weight 900 belongs to headings and to the price on a tile. It is the system's way of writing in marker, and spending it anywhere else makes the board shout.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Money, counts, dates in a column and ticket codes are set with tabular numerals, and money is formatted through one helper (`frontend/src/lib/money.ts`) rather than per page.

rules.name: The Bundled Face Rule
rules.body: Both faces ship with the application. A new face must be added to `@fontsource` and bundled, never referenced from a CDN, and must prove it sits with Nokora in a compact table row and on the printed slip.

rules.name: The Laptop Rule
rules.body: Design at 1366×768. A component that only works at 1920 is wrong here.

rules.name: The Board Header Rule
rules.body: Every surface opens with the same header block and closes it with a 2px ink rule. It is a masthead, not an eyebrow: the club name and the date share a baseline, and the page title sits on the row below.

rules.name: The Register Above The Fold Rule
rules.body: On the sale surface, today's board must begin within the first viewport at the reference size. Tile columns give up height for it.

rules.name: The Two Densities Rule
rules.body: A table is comfortable or compact, chosen once in the density module, never adjusted per cell.

rules.name: The Flat Board Rule
rules.body: If it is a surface, it has no shadow — cards and tables take `border border-rule`. If it is an object on the board, it may. The magnet is the only object.

rules.name: The Marker Stroke Rule
rules.body: A thick line is a marker stroke and means a section boundary or a product's identity. Nothing else gets one; there is no accent border on a card.

rules.name: The Radius Ladder Rule
rules.body: Controls 6px, tables and dialogs 8px, tiles and cards 12px, magnets and chips full. A container never rounds tighter than the control inside it.

rules.name: The Confirming Motion Rule
rules.body: No entrance animation on a table row or a price tile, no attention-seeking loop, no bouncy easing. This is an eight-hour tool with a queue in front of it.

rules.name: The Declared Keyframe Rule
rules.body: An animation class must have a keyframe behind it. Several classes in this codebase once animated nothing at all; a class without a declared keyframe is a defect, and keyframes live in `tailwind.config.cjs` or `index.css`, never inside a page.

dos: take facility colour from `lib/facility.ts` and nowhere else, and let a combination tile show its stripes side by side.
say what state a record is in with a magnet, and what a product is with a marker hue.
keep controls at 36px and page padding at 12px; this is a laptop tool.
put ink lettering on amber, and reserve amber for the one committing action on a surface.
set a product name, a label and a table cell in ink, whatever colour its facility is.
open every surface with the board header and close the block with a 2px ink rule.
keep today's board inside the first viewport on the sale surface, even at the cost of visible tiles.
name a panel's scope when the figures beside it and the rows beneath it come from different queries.
set money through the shared formatter and every compared figure in tabular numerals.
keep soft ink at 38% and the caption step at 1.6 line height, and check a Khmer header before calling a table done.
keep the printed slip black on white with square corners and 2px rules.
donts: declare a facility palette inside a page.
set text in gym green or steam orange; they do not clear 4.5:1 on white.
use amber for a heading, a chip, a border or a background.
use the black weight anywhere but a heading and a tile price.
add a shadow to a card or a table shell. The magnet and the sticky navbar are the only things that lift.
put a thick or coloured border on a card; the 2px section rule and the 3px tile stripe are the only heavy lines.
use an arbitrary `text-[Npx]` size on screen; the printed slip is the only exception.
ship an animation class with no keyframe behind it, or declare a keyframe inside a page.
let a table wrap or shrink its figures on narrow screens; drop columns by priority or stack the row.
design for dark mode. The board is light-only and the stray `.dark` rule that once contradicted the tokens has been removed.
add a fifth icon library. Lucide is the direction of travel; a file being touched moves toward it.
